title: Keystroke Dynamics Patterns While Writing Positive and Negative Opinions
objective: Differentiating positive and negative opinions based on keystroke dynamics patterns during text input.
methodology: Semi-experimental study with 50 participants writing opinions on learning experiences. Keystroke dynamics were captured and over 50 features analyzed for classification accuracy.
dataset: Keystroke data from 50 participants writing opinions on positive/negative learning experiences and teacher interactions.
performance: Classification accuracy slightly above random guess; second approach using self-report labels achieved more accurate results.
limitations: Accuracy could be improved by combining keystroke data with other modalities.

title: Under Pressure: Sensing Stress of Computer Users
objective: Recognizing when computer users are stressed can help reduce their frustration and prevent negative health conditions.
methodology: A within-subjects laboratory study using a pressure-sensitive keyboard and capacitive mouse to detect behavioral changes during stressful tasks.
dataset: 24 participants performing expressive writing, text transcription, and mouse clicking tasks over 30 minutes.
performance: 79% of participants showed increased typing pressure; 75% showed more mouse surface contact during stressful conditions.
limitations: Results are limited to a lab setting and may not generalize to real-world scenarios.

title: The Effect of Emotion on Keystroke: An Experimental Study Using Facial Feedback Hypothesis
objective: To investigate the effect of emotion on keystroke dynamics through controlled experiments under facial feedback-induced emotional states
methodology: Facial feedback hypothesis used to induce emotions via teeth/lip conditions. Keystroke duration and latency analyzed using t-tests on 15 participants' typing data
dataset: 15 university students (mean age 23.4) typed number sequence '67829751' under positive (teeth) and negative (lip) emotional states
performance: Significant differences in keystroke duration/latency between emotional states (p < 0.05). High accuracy in distinguishing positive/negative states
limitations: Small sample size (15 participants) and limited emotional induction methods (facial feedback only)

title: NOT MENTIONED
objective: Review state-of-the-art emotion recognition methods from keystroke, mouse, and touchscreen dynamics, addressing challenges and future directions for non-intrusive emotion detection.
methodology: Systematic literature review of 102 papers focusing on emotion elicitation methods, recognition features, and classification techniques.
performance: Studies show varying accuracy (60-95%) depending on emotion type, feature extraction, and classification methods.
limitations: Limited focus on real-world applications and long-term emotional state tracking.

title: NOT MENTIONED
objective: Understand how individual user features affect emotional changes in response to stimuli or environmental changes, and develop a framework for personalized emotion recognition.
methodology: Conducted a questionnaire survey with 107 participants and data analysis to explore relationships between user features and KMT dynamics features.
limitations: Initial framework focuses only on KMT dynamics; integration of user features into behavioral features remains unclear.
